 Oral Judgment
In this appeal, the petitioner is seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Undisputedly, there was an accident on 27.06.2012.

The petitioner was traveling in the Nano Car bearing No.KA-40-M-2833 along with her husband at 7.30 p.m., near Nelavanki village between Chinthamani-Rayalpadu road, when the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-736 hit against the car,
due to which the inmates of the car sustained the injuries.
The petitioner sustained fractures of both the femur and her husband died at the spot.
After taking treatment, she has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the KSRTC.

Tribunal after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties by impugned judgment and NC:
2024:KHC:38732 award, assessed compensation of Rs.2,38,454/- with interest at 6% per annum.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the argument of Sri. Nanjunda Swamy P.L., learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.
H.R. Renuka, learned counsel for the KSRTC.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that, the petitioner is aged less than 25 years, she is an income tax assessee, Tribunal has taken her notional income only, in spite of medical evidence speaking 20% of whole body disability, the Tribunal considered it only at 8%, no compensation was awarded towards loss of amenities and discomfort and also future medical expenses.
Compensation awarded under different heads is inadequate and sought for enhancement.

6. Per contra learned counsel for the KSRTC has contended that having regard to the medical evidence, NC: 2024:KHC:38732 the disability assessed by the Tribunal is proper, though the PAN Card is shown there is no income tax returns are proof of income that was placed before the Tribunal, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income, compensation awarded under different heads is proper.
It is further contended that though medical evidence speaks of future medical expenses even after 12 years of the accident, the petitioner has not underwent any surgery for removal implants.
Under such circumstances, the Tribunal has rightly not assessed the compensation towards future medical expenses and she supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.

8. The KSRTC is not disputing the accident, the award passed by the Tribunal has already satisfied S A Shravanthi vs The Manager on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49075387/
2 by the KSRTC.

sentences.text: Hence, the point is only regarding the quantum of compensation.
Medical records shows that NC: 2024:KHC:38732 the petitioner has suffered comminuted fracture of right femur and open segmented fracture of middle 1/3rd of left femur.
She was under hospitalization from 28.06.2012 to 30.07.2012 at R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar.
PW-2/Dr.Imran Hussain, Orthopedic Surgeon of R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, is a treated doctor.

His evidence suggest 30% of limb disability sustained by the petitioner for each of her legs and whole body disability is assessed at 20% and it could be taken as functional disability having regard to age and avocation of the petitioner.
9.
The petitioner has not placed any evidence as proof of her income.
Hence, the notional income has to be considered for the year 2012 at Rs.7,000/-.
As regarding age is concerned, the hospital record suggests the age of the petitioner at the time of accident as 25.

Her date of birth is 22.02.1988, on the date of accident as indicated in the PAN Card and Adhar Card, the same is proper and it is taken NC: 2024:KHC:38732 accordingly and the applicable multiplier is '18'.
The petitioner will be laid-up minimum of six months and she has to be compensated for the loss of income.

She underwent ordial of pain and suffering, suffered loss of amenities and discomfort and it has to be compensated.
10.

Considering the totality of the case, nature of injuries and the treatment taken age, avocation of the petitioner is proper to assess Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.40,000/- towards loss amenities and discomfort, medical expenses of Rs.72,174/-, loss of income of six months during the laid-up at Rs.7,000/- comes to Rs.42,000/-.
The petitioner was under hospitalization for 32 days, was attended by an attendant, money spent towards conveyance and also food and nourishment.
Hence, under incidental expenses consolidated Rs.25,000/- is assessed.
Medical evidence suggests Rs.25,000/- to Rs.30,000/- as the future medical expenses for removal of NC: 2024:KHC:38732 implants, hence, Rs.25,000/- will be the future medical expenses.
As regarding loss of future income
Total compensation comes to Rs.5,46,574/- as against Rs.2,38,454/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby, enhancement of Rs.3,08,120/-.

It is the just compensation that,
the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.
11.
